‭Republic of Peru‬
‭I-2‬
‭Putting an End to the Use of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Warfare‬
‭Policy Speech:‬
‭My fellow delegates, Resolution 1-2 gives only three people, all from Peru, control over our AI‬
‭capabilities for combat and defense. This poses a severe security threat, but even if we were to‬
‭dangerously turn a blind eye, the resolution naively assumes that the UN will be able to access all of‬
‭SpaceX’s satellites, which is highly improbable given that SpaceX is a private company. I’ve yet to‬
‭mention the most glaring flaw in this resolution; SpaceX satellites are used to provide internet services,‬
‭not geographic surveillance. This makes them entirely inept to survey the use of AI in warfare, even if the‬
‭UN could secure a contract with SpaceX. For these deep-rooted reasons, in addition to implementing‬
‭punishments that the First Committee has absolutely no right to implement, we cannot support this‬
‭resolution under any circumstances if we hope to preserve our security.‬
‭Key Points:‬
‭●‬ ‭SpaceX satellites are used for internet connectivity, not for geographic surveillance, making them‬
‭incapable of surveying the use of AI in warfare‬
‭●‬ ‭Giving complete control over reviewing the deployment of AI to one nation is grossly‬
‭irresponsible and dangerous‬
‭●‬ ‭It’s very unlikely that SpaceX will grant the UN access to any of its satellites.‬
‭○‬ ‭Further, it’s nearly impossible that it will give access to all of its satellites‬
‭●‬ ‭Still, besides the confidential satellites that have been manufactured for the US military, SpaceX’s‬
‭fleet is entirely comprised of internet satellites‬
‭●‬ ‭DISEC cannot impose fines for non-compliance‬
‭●‬ ‭Even if DISEC could impose fines, amounts of 25-150 million USD are astronomical‬
‭●‬ ‭The resolution wants to completely ban the use of autonomous AI systems in combat‬
‭○‬ ‭Why should systems like these which often prevent unnecessary civilian casualties be‬

content.Diminishing Artificial-Intelligence-Powe:
Resolution 1-3 include some important measures regarding Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems,‬
‭however, some amendments must be made to ensure the safety of this resolution. I applaud the Imperialist‬
‭Satellite State, which some nations may refer to as Israel, for establishing a specific working definition of‬
‭a LAW System and for drawing attention to the use of these systems for non-retaliatory purposes in armed‬
‭conflict zones. Unfortunately, the resolution contradicts itself by stating the positive effects of LAWS,‬
‭including reduced civilian casualties and improved accuracy, and later proclaiming that they hope to‬
‭eliminate all LAW Systems within 15-25 years, and later want to ban AI in combat entirely. I implore the‬
‭author of this paper and other delegates to discuss further how we might improve this resolution because‬
‭the Imperialist Satelite State dangerously uses AI in their combative capabilities with the Iron Dome, so‬
‭this last statement puts us all in imminent danger.‬
‭Key Points:‬
‭Positive:‬
‭●‬ ‭They established a clear and specific definition of LAWS‬
‭●‬ ‭They bring crucial attention to the use of LAW Systems for non-retaliatory purposes in active‬
‭conflict zones‬
‭Negative:‬
‭●‬ ‭They didn't establish who specifically would be a member of‬‭detectives‬
‭●‬ ‭They hope to ban LAWS in all instances instead of strictly for initial offenses‬
‭●‬ ‭They hope to entirely ban the use of AI in warfare‬
‭●‬ ‭Israel hopes to ban LAWS/AI, but they use them in the form of the Iron Dome and Arrow‬
‭●‬ ‭Requires non-compliant state to pay a fine; DISEC does not have the authority to do this‬
‭The French Republic‬
‭1-4‬
‭Managing the Use of Iranian Shahed Drones in the Russia-Ukraine War‬
‭Policy Speech:‬
‭I’d like you to imagine an apocalyptic reality where nations are punished for simply defending‬
‭themselves. Sadly, we won’t have to imagine if this resolution is passed. Resolution 1-4 wants to punish‬
‭Iran for supplying Russia with groundbreaking AI defense technologies that allowed Russia to defend‬
‭itself from Ukraine. Further, this resolution hopes to place sanctions on a private Iranian company,‬
‭however, DISEC nor the UN has the power to place sanctions on a private entity. Lastly, France hopes to‬
‭implement a drone detection system in Ukraine, but a nearly identical system already exists, meaning‬
‭there’s no reason to request nearly 50 million dollars in funding.  I urge the delegate representing France‬
‭and any others who may support this resolution to explain why they specifically want to monitor Iranian‬
‭drones. We can’t allow the French Republic to place uncalled-for surveillance on Iranian drones because‬
‭it’s setting a precedent of surveillance without evidence. If they do this to Iran, any other nation could be‬
‭their next target, which is why we must not support this resolution.‬
‭Key Points:‬
‭●‬ ‭The drones that Iran supplied to Russia were purely used for defensive measures‬
‭●‬ ‭DISEC nor the UN can impose sanctions on a private company‬
‭○‬ ‭DISEC can’t impose any sanctions‬
‭●‬ ‭There’s inadequate evidence to prove that there should be specific surveillance on Iran‬
‭●‬ ‭There’s already a drone defense system in Ukraine that is very similar to the proposed‬‭AirGuard‬
‭Defense System‬‭so the requested 50 million dollars‬‭in funding is futile‬
‭○‬ ‭The World Bank only gives loans for humanitarian purposes, so they likely wouldn’t‬
‭provide funding for the defense system even if it didn’t already exist‬
‭●‬ ‭Referenced resolution A/C.1/78/L.56 in the preambulatory clauses hopes to impose additional‬
‭restrictions on LAWS beyond what’s placed on all other types of weapons‬
‭○‬ ‭Why should there be additional restrictions placed on LAWS when they have been‬
‭proven to have increased accuracy and decreased civilian casualties?‬
‭Key Points of Topic I Committee Discussion‬
‭●‬ ‭Article 51 of the United Nations Charter states that every state has an inherent right to‬
‭self-defense, and LAWS and other combative weapons that use AI are a critical component of‬
‭self-defense for many nations, including North Korea‬
‭○‬ ‭NATO already has “clear pathways” to implement AI-enabled LAWS, so imposing‬
‭additional restrictions on the use of LAWS puts adversaries in grave danger‬
‭○‬ ‭South Korea (Chosun) uses LAWS for self-defense, so North Korea must also be able to‬
‭use LAWS to protect itself‬
‭○‬ ‭Continued conflict with the United States, a nation that has no LAWS regulations, also‬
‭poses a massive threat to the security of North Korea, further emphasizing why LAWS‬
‭and AI-enabled combat and weapons are necessary‬
‭●‬ ‭The Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons clearly states that prior humanitarian law,‬
‭such as the Geneva Convention, also applies to autonomous weapons systems, meaning that‬
‭additional regulation on LAWS is unnecessary and violates previous conventions‬
‭○‬ ‭Further, these conventions have repeatedly been ineffective due to compliance issues,‬
‭corrupt political motivations, and selective compliance‬
‭○‬ ‭An example of this is how Saudi Arabia uses cluster munitions in the Syria civil war‬
‭despite international condemnation‬
‭○‬ ‭We shouldn’t establish additional treaties and conventions since the pre-existing ones are‬
‭ineffective and foster conflict and disobedience‬
‭●‬ ‭The basic principles of sovereignty and non-interference with domestic issues are violated if‬
‭there’s increased surveillance over LAWS and other AI-enabled systems‬
‭○‬ ‭There are major security concerns with increased surveillance‬
‭○‬ ‭Increased surveillance is a violation of a state’s right to privacy‬
‭●‬ ‭DISEC nor any other General Assembly committee has the authority to impose any form of a‬
‭sanction or fine on any state, company, person, or group whatsoever‬
‭○‬ ‭They also don’t have the authority to pass any legally binding laws or regulations‬
